common_name: Cara's Choice Blueberry (Beltsville Aromatic Blueberry, Northern Highbush Blueberry)

planting.note: Plant dormant, container-grown bushes in early spring into strongly acidic, well-drained, organic-rich soil amended with peat or pine bark; set a second early-to-midseason northern highbush cultivar nearby to improve pollination and fruit set.

directions: Cara's Choice was released in 2000 by the cooperative USDA Agricultural Research Service and Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station breeding program at Beltsville, Maryland, bred from a cross carrying diploid, hexaploid, and rabbiteye blueberry relatives and selected chiefly for an unusually complex, aromatic, sweet flavor rather than for size or yield alone. The compact bushes reach only about four to five feet, bear medium powder-blue berries with small dry scars and excellent firmness, and ripen in the early-midseason window while holding their flavor and firmness on the bush for several weeks after coloring. Grow in full sun in strongly acidic (pH 4.5-5.5), well-drained soil and plant a companion cultivar nearby, since cross-pollination improves berry size and set. Its outstanding flavor and compact growth habit have also made it a popular parent in subsequent blueberry breeding work, including the low-chill southern highbush cultivar Gumbo.
sources: Rutgers New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station
